core_obligations: Assume f locally quasi-finite, take a surjective etale U -> X with U a scheme, and conclude that |U_k|, hence |X_k|, is discrete (proof lines 5418-5430).
Conversely choose surjective etale V -> Y and U -> V x_Y X with U, V schemes and note U -> V is locally of finite type (proof lines 5433-5443).
Assuming U -> V is not locally quasi-finite, find a specialization u ~> u' over a common point v of V (proof lines 5444-5447).
Compute the transcendence degrees over kappa(v) and obtain the strict inequality d > d' from the dimension formula for specialisations (proof lines 5451-5454).

Show that u and u' having the same image in |X_v| produces a point of R_v = U_v x_{X_v} U_v making kappa(u) and kappa(u') finite separable over the intermediate field, contradicting d > d' (proof lines 5455-5466).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma characterising local quasi-finiteness of a locally finite type morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces by discreteness of |X_k| for every field-valued point Spec(k) -> Y (source lines 5406-5415). The easy direction reads discreteness off an etale cover; the converse is the substantive one: from a non-locally-quasi-finite U -> V one extracts a specialization u ~> u' lying over the same point v, compares the transcendence degrees d = trdeg_{kappa(v)} kappa(u) and d' = trdeg_{kappa(v)} kappa(u'), uses the scheme case of the dimension formula for specialisations to get d > d', and then shows that assuming u and u' have the same image in |X_v| produces a point r of R_v = U_v x_{X_v} U_v whose residue field is a finite separable extension of both kappa(u) and kappa(u'), forcing d = d'. That contradiction is the heart of the card and cannot be replaced by a formal argument.
